title: Junta Airstrike Near U Raz Mountain Pagoda in Ponnagyun Kills Two, Damages Historic Site
detail: A junta fighter jet dropped bombs near the U Raz Mountain suspension bridge in Ponnagyun Town, Rakhine State, around 12:30 p.m. on September 13, 2026, with one bomb landing on the creek bank and another exploding in the water near passenger motorboats. U Moe Moe, a 65-year-old boat worker from Lay Kan village, and Daw Soe Soe, 37, from Seti Yin village, were killed instantly; three others were injured by shrapnel. A separate bomb struck the upper section of the historic U Yit Taw (Uri Taung) Pagoda, causing partial structural collapse. The strike came amid the SAC's continuing 'Operation 4926' offensive against the Arakan Army around Sittwe and Ponnagyun.

title: KIA-Led Forces Sink or Damage Six Junta Vessels Between Sawati and Mya Lel Villages
detail: KIA-led resistance forces ambushed a flotilla of Military Commission vessels travelling downstream from Bhamo toward Mandalay on the morning of September 13, 2026, between Sawati and Mya Lel villages in Kachin State. Four vessels sank and two were badly damaged by fire. The junta retaliated with at least 15 bombing runs by Y-12 aircraft and fighter jets against Sawati, Kaung Tong and Nyaung Pin Thar villages. Resistance sources say roughly 24 military and cargo vessels have been destroyed and 151 Military Commission personnel captured in the Bhamo river campaign since late August.
